supportGuides.title: Papa Life vs Books and Podcasts on Estrangement
supportGuides.headline: Papa Life vs Books and Podcasts on Estrangement
supportGuides.description: Books and podcasts can offer many perspectives on why families grow apart. Papa Life gives fathers of adult children a sequence of self-paced audio lessons to work through.
supportGuides.intro: Books and podcasts can offer many perspectives on why families grow apart. Papa Life gives fathers of adult children a sequence of self-paced audio lessons to work through.
sections: Choose a book or podcast if you want to hear how other people have experienced estrangement.
Choose a Papa Life lesson if you want to practice listening without defending or taking responsibility for something you did.
Reconciliation is never guaranteed. You can choose how you listen, what you take responsibility for, and how you respect boundaries.

supportGuides.title: Papa Life vs Therapy or Coaching for Adult-Child Distance
supportGuides.headline: Papa Life vs Therapy or Coaching for Adult-Child Distance
supportGuides.description: Papa Life offers self-paced education. Therapy and coaching involve working with a person who can respond to what you tell them.
supportGuides.intro: Papa Life offers self-paced education. Therapy and coaching involve working with a person who can respond to what you tell them.
sections: A licensed therapist can help you work through distress or family conflict. Ask a coach about their training and what support they offer.
A Papa Life lesson lets you reflect privately and on your own schedule. It cannot assess your family or advise you on a specific situation.
Reconciliation is never guaranteed. You can choose how you listen, what you take responsibility for, and how you respect boundaries.

supportGuides.title: Help for Fathers of Estranged Adult Children
supportGuides.headline: Help for Fathers of Estranged Adult Children
supportGuides.description: When your adult child stops calling, you may want to apologize and have no idea what to say. Start with one action you can control.
supportGuides.intro: When your adult child stops calling, you may want to apologize and have no idea what to say. Start with one action you can control.
sections: If your adult child has asked for space, respect that request. Use the time to think about what they told you and what you can take responsibility for.
If contact is welcome, keep it simple. You could say, “I want to understand what this has felt like for you. I’m ready to listen.”
Reconciliation is never guaranteed. You can choose how you listen, what you take responsibility for, and how you respect boundaries.
